rules.statement: When several callers share a single in-flight asynchronous operation, such as a cached retrieval, run the shared operation with `CancellationToken.None` bounded by its own timeout, and have each caller wait on it with `WaitAsync(cancellationToken)`.
rules.why: If one caller's token cancels the shared operation, that caller breaks the retrieval for every other caller waiting on it. With `WaitAsync`, a caller that cancels just stops waiting.
rules.check: Look for code that deduplicates or shares a task across callers, for example a cached `Task`, a `Lazy<Task>` or a dictionary of in-flight tasks, and passes one caller's `CancellationToken` into the shared work. Also flag shared work that has no timeout of its own.

rules.statement: Seal an internal type unless a derived type, or a test reaching it through `InternalsVisibleTo`/`DynamicProxyGenAssembly2`, subclasses or mocks it.
rules.why: CA1852 is enabled with warnings as errors. It flags unsealed internal types only in assemblies that grant no `InternalsVisibleTo`, so mockable internals in assemblies that grant it to their tests can stay unsealed.
rules.check: Look for new internal classes left unsealed in an assembly that has no `InternalsVisibleTo`, and for convention text claiming internal types always stay unsealed.

rules.statement: Keep convention and instruction documents consistent with the analyzer rules the build enforces, and state the exact condition under which an enforced rule applies.
rules.why: A contributor or agent who follows a convention that contradicts an enforced analyzer writes code that fails the build under warnings as errors.
rules.check: When a diff turns an analyzer rule on or off, check that the convention documents describing that behavior are updated so they don't contradict it.
